title: Catalyst Role for Singapore in Addressing Climate Change Issues
what_it_is: Catalyst Role for Singapore in Addressing Climate Change Issues

sections.label: Singapore climate change catalyst role
sections.summary: Asked what catalyst role Singapore can play locally, regionally and internationally to tackle climate change given its small land size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources given Singapore's small land size, what catalyst role can we play on the local, regional and international fronts to tackle climate change.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax and solar
sections.summary: Singapore implemented an economy-wide carbon tax, plans floating solar systems, and targets doubling solar deployment and greening infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Singapore implemented an economy-wide carbon tax last year – the first in Southeast Asia to do so – as a key plank of our mitigation strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will also push the bounds of innovation, such as deploying floating solar photovoltaic systems on our reservoirs and offshore, to make up for our shortage of land area to deploy them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Such innovations have given us confidence to raise our level of ambition to double our solar deployment target from one Gigawatt peak (GWp) beyond 2020 to at least two GWp by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are also greening our physical and transport infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are aiming for 80% of buildings in Singapore to be green by 2030 and for 90% of peak hour commuting trips to be via public transport, active mobility or shared transport by 2040.

sections.label: Paris Agreement emissions commitments
sections.summary: Under the Paris Agreement every country agreed to reduce emissions by 2030 within its own constraints, and will be asked to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, there was always an argument about who started it first, who had a bigger responsibility and who should do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But with the Paris Agreement, every country now has agreed to at least put their best foot forward and try to do what they can do within the constraints of their own country to try and reduce emissions by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: By 2030, we will also be asking all these countries which have agreed to the Paris Agreement framework to do even more.

sections.label: Carbon trading rules failure
sections.summary: The question of trading carbon with countries having extra credits if commitments are not met fell through in the last agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In particular, the last instance, on the trading rules, "how can we – if we do not meet our commitments – be able to trade carbon with countries that have extra credits?" Even though it looks quite mechanical and simple, it fell through in the last agreement.
